subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: For provider-minted signed-thinking fields, should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid opaque replay tokens even when their bytes contain credential-shaped substrings?
rationale: The current tests deliberately redact credential-shaped values in provider signature fields, but the issue shows that this policy can corrupt real opaque replay tokens; maintainer intent is needed for the redaction/security boundary.

options.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
options.body: Preserve valid opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while leaving arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

options.title: Pattern-Only Hardening
options.body: Make fixed-case vendor prefixes and boundaries stricter but keep the current redaction-idempotency requirement for provider signatures.

options.title: Send-Side Recovery Only
options.body: Drop visibly corrupted Bedrock/Anthropic thinking blocks on send and rely on recovery without changing transcript-redaction preservation.

recommendation.title: Scoped Structural Preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve valid opaque signatures only in known provider signed-thinking fields while leaving arbitrary text, missing-route fields, and malformed payloads redacted.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame points to steipete on the central redaction and Bedrock replay surfaces, making him the best available routing owner for the boundary choice.
